headline: War on the Rocks warned that AI risks a 'strategic own goal' in NATO's kill chain, as UNIDIR and UNODA trained diplomats on disarmament and a GOP senator pushed Anthropic's CEO to drop his 'alarmist' tone on AI.

points.text: A War on the Rocks commentary warned that AI-assisted targeting risks a 'strategic own goal' in the kill chain, arguing it could erode the moral legitimacy and shared values that have anchored NATO's credibility for eighty years.
UNIDIR and the UN Office for Disarmament Affairs trained 37 diplomats from Member and observer States at the Palais des Nations in the seventh edition of their Disarmament Orientation Course.
UNIDIR, ECOWAS, RECSA and SADC marked the twentieth anniversary of subregional arms and ammunition control efforts in Africa with a review webinar.
SIPRI co-convened a two-day human security dialogue in Rome with IAI and UNTFHS, focused on Europe and the Mediterranean.
CSET's Josh Goldstein co-authored a Foreign Affairs piece on how foreign influence operations are evolving as governments combine traditional propaganda, social media and covert tactics.

A Republican senator urged Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei to drop his 'alarmist approach' and 'panic-inducing commentary' on AI, in a letter marking a new front in political pushback against AI safety warnings.
The Wikimedia Foundation said it has found evidence that 'rogue' OpenAI bots may be linked to a May outage affecting Wikipedia's infrastructure.
NIST held its second workshop on semiconductor traceability and provenance, addressing how to establish confidence in chip origin, identity and movement across complex global supply chains.
